Here's a self-contained prompt for a fresh session in ~/projects/readaloud:

# Task: multi-chapter offline prefetch horizon for the readaloud audio player

## Context (read first)
Memory files (auto-loaded) — read fully before touching code:
- `project_incident_2026-08-18_commute_pullback.md` (the "Still open" paragraph is this task)
- `project_incident_2026-06-11_commute_autoplay.md`
- `project_playback_state_reconciliation.md` (the architecture rules; non-negotiable)

Commit `157874b` fixed the rejoin pull-back. What's left from the 2026-08-18 commute
is the **13:49:25 stall**: with the screen off, Android cut the page's network from
~13:43:30 to 13:49:32 (WS dead, `fetch` → "TypeError: Failed to fetch",
`navigator.onLine` never went false). The next-chapter prefetch is triggered at 15%
of the current chapter and only reaches ONE chapter ahead, so the blackout spanned
the whole prefetch window for chapter 16809: playback reached the end of 16808 with
no blob, `swapToChapter` targeted the network URL, `audio-stalled`, silence until
the user woke the phone. A 2–3-chapter horizon prefetched during 16807 (online at
13:40) would have carried the chain through.

## Goal
Make the offline autoplay chain survive a network blackout of at least two full
chapters: keep the next **N=3** chapters' audio blobs + `/nav` windows in memory,
start filling as soon as a chapter starts (not at 15%), and let the chain consume
them without any server round-trip.

## Where the code is
`apps/readaloud_web/assets/js/hooks/audio_player.ts`:
- Single-slot prefetch state ~L555–660: `currentBlobUrl`, `prefetchedBlobUrl`,
  `prefetchedFor`, `prefetchAbort`, `prefetchedNav`, `fetchPrefetchNav`,
  `tryStartPrefetch`.
- Consumer: `clientNavigate` ~L780–850 (uses the blob iff `prefetchedFor ===
  target.networkUrl`, adopts `prefetchedNav` into `CHAPTER_WINDOW`, revokes
  `currentBlobUrl`, resets the slot).
- Trigger: `timeupdate` handler ~L1142 (`PREFETCH_TRIGGER_FRACTION = 0.15`).
- `navTarget()` reads ONLY the client-owned `CHAPTER_WINDOW` WeakMap
  (`lib/chapter_window.ts`, `/api/books/:b/chapters/:c/nav` → `parseChapterWindow`).
- Diagnostics: `log("prefetch-*")` events; every new event name must be added to
  `@known_events` in `apps/readaloud_web/lib/readaloud_web_web/player_events.ex`.
- `retryPendingAutoplay` (`online`/`visibility-visible`) is the recovery path when the
  chain runs past the horizon — keep it working.

## Design constraints
- Replace the single slot with a small cache keyed by network audio URL: entry =
  `{blobUrl, nav: ChapterWindow|null, abort}`; walk forward from the loaded chapter
  via each entry's `nav.next` to fill up to N; revoke blobs when the loaded chapter
  moves past them or a manual jump makes them unreachable; abort in-flight fetches
  that become unreachable. Bound memory (chapters are ~15–20 MB WAV; 3 ahead ≈ 60 MB
  — acceptable, don't go higher). Prev-direction blobs are out of scope.
- Fill trigger: on mount and on every swap (immediately), plus retry on `online` /
  `visibility-visible` and on `timeupdate` (throttled) so a failed fetch retries.
- Follow the reconciliation memory: `swapToChapter` stays the ONLY `audio.src`
  writer; `navTarget` stays `CHAPTER_WINDOW`-only; on swap the window advances from
  the consumed entry's `nav` (or goes empty — never stale). No new writers, no
  per-edge patches.
- Keep every existing `prefetch-*` event semantics where they still apply; add
  e.g. `prefetch-cache-evict`, `prefetch-horizon` (depth reached) — and add
  `navigator.onLine` + `connection?.effectiveType` to `prefetch-fail`/`prefetch-nav-fail`
  detail (we couldn't tell blackout from Doze in the incident logs).
- Add a Prometheus-visible signal only if trivial; logs are the priority.

## Tests — IMPORTANT: the e2e VM run is ~5 min. Do at most TWO runs total:
one to see the new test red (optional if you're confident), one green at the end.
- Extend `e2e/tests/autoplay-offline-chain.test.js` (read it fully — the fixture is
  3 chapters, all with audio; `AUDIO_FIXTURE_FILE` hiding + `page.setOfflineMode`
  is how "offline" is simulated; note media-element requests bypass CDP emulation)
  or add a sibling test: after mounting ch1 online with autoplay, wait for
  `prefetch-done` for BOTH ch2 and ch3, go offline (hide the file too), dispatch
  `ended` twice, and assert ch2 → ch3 both swap to `blob:` sources with no
  `audio-stalled`/`prefetch-fail`-driven stop and no `nav-blocked-*`. If the fixture
  needs a 4th chapter to prove the horizon *ends* correctly, extend
  `ReadaloudAudiobook.Fixtures.E2E.seed!/1` (`audio_for`) — don't `t.skip`.
- `mix precommit` and `mix assets.typecheck` must pass; ast-grep/lint-grep/treefmt run
  in the pre-commit hook. `git add` new files before `mix test.e2e` (flake needs them).
- Verification before claiming done: paste the e2e spec summary line.

## Deliverable
One conventional commit on master (`feat(reader): …` or `fix(reader): …`), then push,
`nix flake update readaloud` in `~/projects/configs`, `deploy --on pylon`, confirm the
new bundle serves (curl the app.js for a new event name), commit the configs
`flake.lock` bump (that repo's format-check hook rewrites unrelated files and fails on
a pre-existing parse error — restore them and use `--no-verify` for the lock-only
commit). Update the incident memory's "Still open" paragraph when done.

Do NOT touch `reprioritize_pending_jobs` / busy_timeout in this task.

Two things I'd add if you want them as separate follow-ups later: the reprioritize_pending_jobs write-lock hog (json_extract scan of oban_jobs per handle_params), and a Grafana panel over the new lv-reconnected / rejoin-reassert-chapter counters so a pull-back regression shows up without log archaeology.
I'll start by reading the three memory files, then the audio player hook and the e2e test.

name: incident-2026-08-18-commute-pullback
description: "8/18/2026 commute — audio pulled BACKWARDS 3× on screen-wake because LV rejoin uses stale View.href (client pushState doesn't update it), and syncAudioToDataset trusts the rehydration diff as a server-owned nav"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 087e6694-3a24-4799-abbc-be0cad08e97f

2026-08-18 13:37–14:10 UTC, book 22 (Shadow Slave), chapters 16806–16814 (Ch 2303–2311). Journal + client events in pylon journald (`[player]` lines).

**Root cause of the pull-backs (13:49:33 → 16806, 13:55:18 → 16808, 14:05:50 → 16808):**
Phoenix LiveView's JS `View.href` is what the `lv:` channel sends as `url` on every (re)join. It is set only at page load, `onLivePatch` (server push_patch delivered), and `pushLinkPatch`. Our client-owned nav does raw `history.pushState` (audio_player.ts `clientNavigate`) → `view.href` stays at the *page-load* URL. Server `advance_chapter already-current (client-owned)` skips push_patch, so href never advances. WS dies on screen-off (every time), LV process times out, screen-on → rejoin → server mounts the page-load chapter → dataset transition → `syncAudioToDataset` treats it as a server-owned move and swaps audio backwards. `force-reconnect` (app.ts) comment claims remount uses "current URL" — false, same stale href. `liveSocket.disconnect()/connect()` keeps existing root views (joinRootViews only setHref for new roots).

**Secondary:** (1) network dead while screen off ~13:43:30–13:49:32 with no `net-offline` (navigator.onLine stayed true → likely Android background/Doze restriction, not signal loss); prefetch (starts at 15% of chapter, 1-chapter horizon) failed → chain stalled at 13:49:25 until user woke phone. (2) `Exqlite.Error Database busy` crashed ReaderLive twice (13:50:18, 14:05:54) — beacon POST progress + LV progress_observations + `reprioritize_pending_jobs` writing simultaneously on rejoin; busy_timeout is the ecto_sqlite3 default 2s. (3) Page reloads at 13:50:16 and 14:05:54 (page-hide→mount, no lv-reload-deferred) — probably user pull-to-refresh, cause unproven.

**Fixed 2026-08-19 (readaloud 157874b, deployed to pylon):** `readaloud:client-pushstate` event → app.ts `liveSocket.main.setHref(url)`; hook context `onDisconnected/onReconnected`; `rejoinPending` guard in `syncAudioToDataset` re-asserts LOADED_CHAPTER with a pivot instead of swapping (LV applies the rejoin patch → `updated()` BEFORE `reconnected()`, so arm on disconnect); busy_timeout 15s; events `lv-disconnected/lv-reconnected/rejoin-reassert-chapter`; e2e `autoplay-reconnect-pullback.test.js` (2 cases). **Still open:** prefetch horizon is 1 chapter, single-slot (`prefetchedBlobUrl/prefetchedFor/prefetchedNav` in audio_player.ts), triggered at 15% of the chapter — a screen-off network blackout spanning that window stalls the chain (13:49:25 stall). Needs a multi-slot 2–3 chapter cache; `reprioritize_pending_jobs` json_extract scan of oban_jobs per handle_params is the likely lock holder behind Database busy.

Related: [[incident-2026-06-11-commute-autoplay]] (same WS-death class; that fix made the offline chain work but left the rejoin path).

name: incident-2026-06-11-commute-autoplay
description: Root cause of the 6/11/2026 commute autoplay failure — stale client dataset after WS death makes ended-handler self-swap to the finished chapter; forensics lost to 2-min event prune + sendBeacon clear-on-queue
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 89c980cb-26d4-445b-82ba-1f08d74a3d41
---

2026-06-11 ~13:06–13:40 UTC (9–9:40am EDT), book 12 (Reverend Insanity), chapters 821–825 = chapter_ids 4017–4021.

**Incident 1 (823 didn't autostart, text stuck on 821):** WS died at the exact moment of the 821→822 client-owned autoplay swap (13:14:44; Bandit timeout 13:16:44), so the server's reconciled LV diff never reached the phone. 822 played fully from its prefetched blob offline, but the hook's `ctx.dataset` still said current=4017/next=4018. At 822's end, `navTarget("next")` returned **4018 — the chapter that just finished** — and `swapToChapter` set src to its network URL while offline → `NETWORK_NO_SOURCE`, silence, plus `writeLastPosition(4018, 0)` clobbering the position cache. Fossil evidence: visibility-visible at 13:22:39 with `srcKind=url, networkState=3, readyState=0, currentTime=0`.

**Incident 2 ("824 stuck"):** 824 (4020) actually played fully (steady 30s heartbeats to 721s/725s; WAV has no silent gaps). WS died again at ~13:38:30 right at 824's end; 825 (4021, blob prefetched) presumably autoplayed and halted ~1–2 min in — unobservable server-side.

**Forensics gaps found:** `player_event_buffer.ts` prunes the localStorage backlog at `BACKLOG_PRUNE_AGE_MS = 120_000` (2 min) — including at mount, *before* replay — and `flushViaBeacon` clears the backlog when `sendBeacon` merely queues (returns true even offline). Both buffers lost the entire offline window.

**Fixes shipped (same day, session 89c980cb):** (A) prefetch bundle now also fetches `/api/books/:b/chapters/:c/nav` (new endpoint, `ChapterNeighbors` shared with ReaderLive) and the resulting `CHAPTER_WINDOW` WeakMap is the ONLY source `navTarget` reads — dataset neighbors are adopted only when `LOADED_CHAPTER` matches `ctx.dataset.chapterId` (`adoptDatasetWindow`); on swap the window advances from the prefetched nav or goes empty (empty blocks gracefully, stale navigates wrong). (B) `clientNavigate` self-swap guard (`nav-blocked-self-swap`). (C) `pendingAutoplay` intent set on every autoplay swap, cleared only by the `playing` event; `retryPendingAutoplay` re-swaps from the network URL on `online`/`visibility-visible`. (D) both buffers: confirmed-delivery flush (`confirmed_flush.ts`, only 2xx'd entries leave the backlog), prune 30min/10min, replay-before-prune at mount, `online` flush trigger, plus best-effort beacon on pagehide. E2E: `autoplay-offline-chain.test.js` pins the second offline boundary + online recovery; fixture `audio_for` default is now `[1, 2, 3]`.

Related: [[playback-state-reconciliation]] — this incident is the dataset-replica (server projection) being unable to advance offline while the autoplay chain is designed to run offline.

name: playback-state-reconciliation
description: "readaloud chapter/playback state is replicated 5 ways; fixes must go through the owner/projection/reconciler architecture, never as per-writer edge patches"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 72187cdc-53e9-4b07-8a24-5499cc3b615b
---

The reader's "current chapter + position" is replicated state (audio.src,
URL, LV assigns/text, DB progress row, MediaSession) with ~7 writers over
unreliable channels. Every historical bug (c3ca323, 1788994, the
2026-06-11 wedged-socket incident) was one writer updating a subset of
replicas. The fix (June 2026) is level-triggered reconciliation, not
per-writer patches.

**Why:** edge-triggered "when X happens also update Y" can never be
complete over a wedged WebSocket; a missed edge stays wrong forever.

**How to apply:** when touching chapter nav or playback state, route
through the existing pieces instead of adding a new imperative update:
- Client owner: `LOADED_CHAPTER` WeakMap + `swapToChapter` (the ONLY
  audio.src writer) in `audio_player.ts`; user navs go through
  `clientNavigate`.
- Client reconciler: `syncAudioToDataset` (onUpdate, dataset-transition
  triggered) makes audio follow any server-owned nav — new server navs
  need zero audio handling.
- Server reconciler: `reconcile_chapter_assigns` in `reader_live.ex`
  converges assigns onto the newest **pivot-flagged** observation in each
  `progress_observations` batch. Two hard-won rules: (1) only explicit
  pivots reconcile — position ticks for the old chapter are legitimately
  in flight during server-owned jumps and would drag assigns backwards;
  (2) nav events (`next_chapter` etc.) carry an ABSOLUTE `chapter_id` —
  relative "advance from current" double-steps when the pivot observation
  outruns the nav event on the same socket.
- Wedged-socket detection: `watchNavAck` (lib/nav_ack.ts) → 8s no-ack →
  `readaloud:force-reconnect` (handled in app.ts).
- Chapter graph (the 6th replica, added after [[incident-2026-06-11-commute-autoplay]]):
  neighbor knowledge lives in the client-owned `CHAPTER_WINDOW` WeakMap,
  fed by the prefetch bundle's `/nav` fetch and gated dataset adoption
  (`adoptDatasetWindow` — only when LOADED_CHAPTER == dataset.chapterId).
  `navTarget` never reads the dataset directly. Offline autoplay intent
  is `pendingAutoplay` + `retryPendingAutoplay` (level-triggered on
  online/visible, cleared by `playing` evidence).
- Divergence is observable: `state-divergence` player event on the 30s
  heartbeat; `chapter_advance{mode="reconcile"}` Prometheus counter.

A "wedged" socket (open but not delivering; pushes buffer silently for
20s+) is a real, recurring state on mobile — design for it, don't assume
connected/disconnected binary.

The readaloud project deploys to pylon as a NixOS module via flake input from GitHub. The full loop:

**1. Test**
- `direnv exec . mix compile --warnings-as-errors` from project root — fast sanity check.
- For real tests: `direnv exec . env MIX_ENV=test mix test apps/<app>/test/<file>.exs`. Umbrella-root `mix test` is brittle (per-app DBs need migrations) — prefer per-file invocation. The library/reader tests fail under per-app `mix test` because each spawns its own bare DB; ignore unless directly touched.
- Test DB needs migrations: `direnv exec . env MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.create && mix ecto.migrate`.
- `mix precommit` (alias) runs `compile --warnings-as-errors`, `deps.unlock --unused`, `format`, `test`. Note: format will reformat unrelated files — split those into a separate "chore: mix format" commit before the feature commit.

**2. Commit**
- Lefthook pre-commit runs ast-grep, lint-grep, treefmt (`--fail-on-change`). Treefmt scans all files, so any unformatted file blocks the commit.
- Commit-msg uses conform (conventional commits). Prefix with `feat(scope):`, `fix(scope):`, `chore:` etc. Keep header under ~70 chars.

**3. Deploy**
- Push to GitHub master: `git push origin master` (the configs flake input is `github:ngngardner/readaloud`).
- In `/home/noah/projects/configs/`: `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix flake update readaloud` to bump the lock.
  - Note: the configs project's direnv shell does NOT include `nix` itself — call `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix` directly.
- Deploy: `cd /home/noah/projects/configs && /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix develop --command bash -c "deploy --on pylon"`. The `deploy` shell command wraps `colmena apply --impure --on <hosts>`.
- Watch for `Activation successful` and `All done!` from pylon. The `readaloud.service` systemd unit gets restarted in the `starting the following units:` line.

**3b. Poke the running node (RPC)**
- `readaloud eval` boots a fresh node and dies on missing `SECRET_KEY_BASE`. Use
  `rpc`, which attaches to the live one.
- The release path isn't on PATH; find it via
  `grep -ao '/nix/store/[a-z0-9]*-readaloud[^ "]*' $(systemctl show readaloud.service --property=ExecStart | grep -o '/nix/store/[^ ]*readaloud-start')`.
- `rpc` needs `RELEASE_COOKIE=readaloud RELEASE_TMP=/tmp/readaloud-rpc` in the env.
- Multi-line scripts: write a `.exs` and `Code.eval_file/1` it, but put it under
  `/var/lib/readaloud/` — the unit has PrivateTmp, so `/tmp` paths are invisible
  to it. Escaping Elixir inside nested ssh+bash quoting breaks on `$`; use a file.
- Confirm a deploy actually landed by checking for a symbol only the new build has
  (`function_exported?(Mod, :fun, 1)`) rather than trusting "Activation successful".
  Grepping the .beam for new strings does NOT work (BEAM chunks are compressed).
- `ReadaloudAudiobook.generate_for_chapter/3` does NOT default model/voice from
  the book's `audio_preferences` — pass `model:`/`voice:` explicitly or the task
  is created with empty ones.

**4. Verify**
- Smoke: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://pylon:4000/` should return 200.
- Browser: use Claude-in-Chrome MCP against `http://pylon:4000/`.

**Browser verification recipe (Claude-in-Chrome MCP):**
1. `tabs_context_mcp createIfEmpty=true` once to get a `tabId` (and create a tab if none exists).
2. `browser_batch` for chained navigate + screenshot — saves round-trips.
3. To click DaisyUI dropdown triggers (`<div tabindex="0" role="button">`), use `find` to get a ref then `computer left_click ref=...`. Coordinate clicks on these can miss focus and the popover won't open.
4. To pick a `<select>` value, prefer `form_input` (works reliably **when the select is inside a `<form>` tag**). For phx-change selects rendered outside a form, form serialization is broken — but that's a code bug to fix (wrap in `<form phx-change=... phx-submit=...>`), not a test workaround.
5. `find query="..."` returns refs and (when the select is closed) lists its option text in the description — handy for asserting voice/model lists without opening the dropdown.

**Useful queries:**
- Books with audio activated: `SELECT id, title, audio_preferences FROM books WHERE audio_preferences IS NOT NULL`
- Books without audio (good for testing Set up audio): `SELECT id, title FROM books WHERE audio_preferences IS NULL LIMIT 5`
- DB path on pylon: `/var/lib/readaloud/data/readaloud.db`
- Service: `systemctl status readaloud` on pylon (root@pylon SSH).
- LocalAI URL the running service uses: `systemctl show readaloud.service --property=Environment | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -i localai`

name: readaloud-ci-gotchas
description: "readaloud CI quirks — coverage gate fails on master (~15% vs 80% threshold), flake src excludes untracked files, three mix FOD hashes"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project

Three readaloud CI facts that look like regressions but aren't (verified 2026-06-10):

1. **The Nix coverage gate fails on master.** `checks.x86_64-linux.coverage` has `threshold = 80` but master measures ~14.95% total line coverage (the metrics/logging branch raised it to ~27.87%). `nix flake check` therefore can NEVER fully pass until coverage is actually built out — judge branches by "did coverage go up" + all other checks green, not by flake-check exit code.

2. **Flake checks build from `inputs.self`, which excludes untracked files in a dirty tree.** `git add` new files before trusting any `nix build .#checks...` result, or the check silently runs against incomplete source (esbuild "Could not resolve" errors are the symptom).

3. **Three mix-deps FOD hashes must be updated when mix.lock changes:** prod in `cells/app/packages/readaloud/default.nix`, dev + test in `cells/app/checks/default.nix`. Set each to `""`, build (`.#packages.x86_64-linux.readaloud.passthru.mixFodDeps`, `.#checks…credo`, `.#checks…coverage`), paste the `got:` hashes.

Also: `lazy_html` (LV-test HTML parser) compiles vendored lexbor via git-clone at build time; the coverage check pre-seeds that checkout from `fetchFromGitHub` (see coverage.nix) — if lazy_html's pinned `@lexbor_git_sha` changes on upgrade, update `lexborGitSha` + hash there too.

4. **`MIX_ENV=dev` is exported in the shell profile on phanteks.** A bare `mix test` inherits it and runs ExUnit against the dev repo config (sandbox error: "cannot invoke sandbox operation with pool DBConnection.ConnectionPool"). Always run `MIX_ENV=test mix test` (and `MIX_ENV=test mix precommit`) explicitly.

name: morphdom strips runtime-added DOM attributes
description: Phoenix LiveView's morphdom removes data-* and other attributes that are not declared in the server-rendered template, even on phx-update="ignore" elements. Use JS expando properties (e.g. el.__myMarker) for runtime-only markers that need to survive a re-render.
type: feedback
originSessionId: c098d994-4b88-45a9-979b-ef3874e4e481
---
Phoenix LiveView's morphdom removes attributes from a DOM element if those
attributes are not declared in the freshly server-rendered HTML — including
data-* attributes you added from JS at runtime. This applies even to
elements with `phx-update="ignore"`: that flag preserves the element's
*children* across patches, but does **not** preserve runtime-added
attributes on the element itself.

**Why:** Cost me a wrong-path debug session in the audio-player puppeteer
test. I marked `<audio id="audio-element">` (which has phx-update="ignore")
with `el.dataset.testMarker = "..."` to assert it was the same DOM node
after a chapter swap. The marker was gone after the LV push_patch — not
because the element was replaced (it wasn't), but because morphdom stripped
the unknown data-* attribute when it diffed the server's template.

**How to apply:** When you need a runtime-only DOM marker that must survive
a LiveView re-render, use a JS expando property on the element instead of
an attribute: `el.__readaloudTestMarker = "..."`. Properties live on the
JS object, not in the DOM attribute list, so morphdom never sees them.

Same trick is useful for hook state you want tied to the element lifetime
without polluting the DOM (or risk colliding with morphdom).

**Corollary (2026-06-11): morphdom REPLACES id-less elements, killing
their event listeners.** Elements with a DOM id are patched in place
(node identity + listeners survive); elements without one — e.g. a `:for`
list of buttons — get replaced on the next LV update, silently discarding
any listeners a hook attached to them at mount. This made the chapter-bar
pill clicks dead in production (listeners died on the first
`:fetch_catalog` re-render). Fix: delegate from the hook root
(`ctx.on(ctx.el, "click", e => e.target.closest("[data-x]") ...)`), which
is id-stable — never bind listeners to id-less template children. See
[[playback-state-reconciliation]].

name: push_patch URL needs WS delivery
description: Server-side push_patch only updates the browser URL when the LV diff actually reaches the client; for autoplay-style chapter advance, the JS hook must update the URL itself
type: feedback
originSessionId: bd624c69-1d74-429c-af78-aee1df15b2a4
---
`push_patch(socket, to: ...)` updates server-side `socket.assigns.live_action`/URL state, but the browser URL only physically changes when the LV diff is delivered over the WebSocket. If the WS is suspended (mobile screen lock) and the server-side LV process times out before the diff is sent, the patch is lost — server log says "push_patch to=N+1" but the client URL stays at N.

**Why:** Confirmed in May 2026 from prod server logs after the autoplay-stranding bug. Server logged `next_chapter push_patch to=1152`; the very next entry was `reader-live mount connected chapter_id=1151` — the reconnect mount used the stale browser URL. With `<audio phx-update="ignore">` surviving the remount, audio.src was 1152 while URL was 1151, stranding the user. Required refresh + manual nav to recover.

**How to apply:** When a JS hook drives a chapter/page change that must survive WS hiccups (audio.ended autoplay, lock-screen next/prev), update the URL client-side via `history.pushState` BEFORE pushing the event to the server. Tell the server (via an event payload flag like `url_already_patched: true`) to skip its own `push_patch` so a connected client doesn't get a duplicate history entry. Manual phx-click button paths can keep the original server-driven push_patch — the WS is, by definition, alive when those clicks happen.

defmodule ReadaloudWebWeb.PlayerEvents do
  @moduledoc """
  Ingest boundary for client-side audio-player diagnostic events.

  The JS `playerEventBuffer` mirrors every `[autoplay]` console log line —
  plus visibility/page-lifecycle/network transitions and playback heartbeats
  — to the server, over the LiveView socket while it's alive and via
  `navigator.sendBeacon` when it isn't (mobile screen lock). Both transports
  land here. Each event becomes:

    * one structured `[player]` log line (info level) carrying the client
      wall-clock timestamp, chapter id, audio position, and a sanitized
      detail map — journald ships these to Loki, where they can be lined up
      against the server-side `[autoplay]` traces to reconstruct exactly
      what a sleeping phone did;
    * one bump of the `readaloud_player_event_count` Prometheus counter,
      tagged by event name and transport.

  Counter labels are bounded: only whitelisted event names become label
  values, anything else is counted as `"other"` (and `"malformed"` for
  entries that don't even have an `event` string). The raw name still
  appears in the log line. Duplicate delivery is possible by design (the
  client buffer re-beacons recent events rather than risk losing them), so
  treat counter rates as approximate; logs carry the client timestamp for
  exact forensics.
  """

  require Logger

  @max_events_per_batch 100
  @max_detail_pairs 20
  @max_string_length 300

  # Must cover every event name the audio_player hook can emit (see
  # assets/js/hooks/audio_player.ts). Unknown names are counted as "other".
  @known_events ~w(
    mount destroy set-initial-src preserve-existing-src
    swap-to-chapter swap-play-ok swap-play-blocked
    prefetch-start prefetch-done prefetch-fail prefetch-aborted
    prefetch-abort-stale prefetch-revoke-stale prefetch-discard-target-changed
    prefetch-nav-done prefetch-nav-fail
    go-to-next-chapter go-to-prev-chapter
    next-chapter-blocked-no-target prev-chapter-blocked-no-target
    nav-blocked-self-swap window-adopt autoplay-retry
    history-pushstate push-event
    media-session-nexttrack media-session-previoustrack
    nav-next-chapter-event nav-prev-chapter-event
    audio-play audio-pause audio-ended audio-error
    audio-stalled audio-waiting audio-loadedmetadata audio-seeked
    visibility-hidden visibility-visible page-show page-hide
    page-freeze page-resume net-online net-offline
    lv-reload-deferred lv-reload-resumed
    heartbeat
    sync-audio-to-dataset state-divergence restore-position
    nav-ack-timeout force-reconnect
    lv-disconnected lv-reconnected rejoin-reassert-chapter
  )

  @doc """
  Log + count a batch of raw client events for `book_id`. `transport` is
  `"ws"` (LiveView channel) or `"beacon"` (HTTP fallback). Batches above
  #{@max_events_per_batch} events are truncated with a warning.
  """
  @spec ingest(integer(), [map()] | term(), String.t()) :: :ok
  def ingest(book_id, raw_events, transport) when is_list(raw_events) do
    {events, overflow} = Enum.split(raw_events, @max_events_per_batch)

    if overflow != [] do
      Logger.warning(
        "[player] dropping #{length(overflow)} events over batch cap " <>
          "book_id=#{book_id} transport=#{transport}"
      )
    end

    Enum.each(events, &ingest_one(book_id, &1, transport))
  end

  def ingest(book_id, _raw_events, transport) do
    Logger.warning("[player] non-list events payload book_id=#{book_id} transport=#{transport}")
    :ok
  end

  defp ingest_one(book_id, %{"event" => name} = event, transport) when is_binary(name) do
    emit(metric_label(name), transport)

    Logger.info(fn ->
      detail = event |> Map.get("detail") |> sanitize_detail()

      "[player] event=#{sanitize_string(name)} book_id=#{book_id} " <>
        "chapter_id=#{scalar_field(event, "chapter_id")} " <>
        "position_ms=#{scalar_field(event, "position_ms")} " <>
        "at=#{scalar_field(event, "at")} transport=#{transport} detail=#{inspect(detail)}"
    end)
  end

  defp ingest_one(book_id, _event, transport) do
    emit("malformed", transport)
    Logger.warning("[player] malformed event book_id=#{book_id} transport=#{transport}")
  end

  defp emit(label, transport) do
    :telemetry.execute(
      [:readaloud, :player, :event],
      %{count: 1},
      %{event: label, transport: transport}
    )
  end

  defp metric_label(name) when name in @known_events, do: name
  defp metric_label(_name), do: "other"

  # Client-controlled input goes into log lines — clamp it. Scalars only,
  # strings truncated, pair count capped.
  defp sanitize_detail(detail) when is_map(detail) do
    detail
    |> Enum.filter(fn {k, v} -> is_binary(k) and scalar?(v) end)
    |> Enum.take(@max_detail_pairs)
    |> Map.new(fn {k, v} -> {sanitize_string(k), sanitize_scalar(v)} end)
  end

check_grep() {
    local pattern="$1" include="$2" msg="$3"
    local matches
    if matches=$(${gnugrep}/bin/grep -rn "$pattern" --include="$include" --exclude-dir=deps --exclude-dir=_build --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=worktrees . 2>/dev/null); then
      echo "ERROR: $msg"
      echo "$matches"
      ((errors++)) || true
    fi
  }

  # no-flash-group-outside-layouts
  flash_matches=$(${findutils}/bin/find . -name '*.heex' ! -name '*layout*' ! -path '*/layouts/*' ! -path '*/deps/*' ! -path '*/_build/*' \
    -exec ${gnugrep}/bin/grep -ln '<\.flash_group' {} + 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$flash_matches" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: <.flash_group> must only be used inside layouts."
    echo "$flash_matches"
    ((errors++)) || true
  fi

  # no-form-for-changeset
  check_grep \
    '<\.form.*for={@changeset}' \
    '*.heex' \
    'Never pass @changeset to <.form>. Use to_form/2 to create @form first.'

  # no-form-let
  check_grep \
    '<\.form.*let={' \
    '*.heex' \
    '<.form let={f}> is deprecated. Use <.form for={@form}> and @form[:field].'

  # no-enum-each-in-heex
  check_grep \
    'Enum\.each' \
    '*.heex' \
    "Don't use Enum.each in HEEx. Use for comprehension: <%= for item <- @items do %>."

  # no-css-apply
  check_grep \
    '@apply ' \
    '*.css' \
    "Don't use @apply in CSS. Write Tailwind classes directly on elements."

  # no-is-prefix-functions
  is_matches=$(${gnugrep}/bin/grep -rEn '^\s*(def|defp)\s+is_' --include='*.ex' --include='*.exs' --exclude-dir=deps --exclude-dir=_build --exclude-dir=worktrees . 2>/dev/null \
    | ${gnugrep}/bin/grep -v 'defguard' || true)
  if [ -n "$is_matches" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Predicate functions should end with ? not start with is_. Reserve is_ for guards."
    echo "$is_matches"
    ((errors++)) || true
  fi

  # no-nested-modules
  while IFS= read -r file; do
    count=$(${gnugrep}/bin/grep -c '^defmodule ' "$file" 2>/dev/null) || count=0
    if [ "$count" -gt 1 ]; then
      echo "ERROR: Multiple top-level modules in $file — causes cyclic dependencies."
      ((errors++)) || true
    fi

  if [ "$errors" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "Found $errors grep lint error(s)."
    exit 1
  fi
